clauses.text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Frank B. Bourn, Chief of the Supplies and Accounts Division, Office of the Secretary of War, War Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1939, by Executive Order No. 7863 of April 7, 1938, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Frank B. Bourn from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1940.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

versions.research_rationale:
EO 8106 (May 3, 1939) exempts Frank B. Bourn from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1940", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on June 30, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. Later extension orders are recorded as later events and do not end this order's clause. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

A repeat search by the producer of all held order texts for this order's number (the forms \"No. 8106\" and \"Executive Order(s) ... 8106\") found only these held order texts citing this order by number, each read in full: EO 8420; it is a further exemption of the same employee and does not revoke, amend or supersede this order. The packet's Federal Register disposition-note search (checked 2026-10-19) reported 1 hit for this order (the notes on EO 8420). The person-name search over held order texts (checked 2026-10-28) reported 1 hit (the same extension order). The packet's U.S. Code and eCFR searches (checked 2026-10-17) found no hit for this order. No held source shows a repeal or change of section 204 before June 30, 1940, and a general statute that did not name this order would be only a disclosed candidate under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments, not an end. The held record contains no separation or death date for the employee and none is needed: the permission was stated for a fixed period, so the stated end is the earliest end the held evidence supports.","independent_command_check":"The order contains a single operative command, the exemption itself; the recital is the President's stated judgment on which the exemption rests and is not a separate command. The complete held text (one recital paragraph, one operative paragraph and the signature line) was read, and the inventory of one operative clause is complete."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
